Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The unemployment rate of 7.8% with the fed funds rate near 0.12% points to early 2013. The 10-year yield at 2.03% and a VIX of 14.3 fit the same period.

Unemployment was 7.8% in both September 2012 and January 2013. Looking at the 10-year yield, it was about 1.6-1.7% in late 2012 and rose to about 2.0% by Feb 2013. The 3-month change of +0.31 therefore suggests a date of January to March 2013.

Other figures support this. US large-cap equities returned +5.1% in the latest month, which matches January 2013 (S&P up about 5%). Treasuries fell 1.3% in the month, and the 20y+ sector fell 3.2%, which also matches January 2013. Unemployment was 7.9% in January 2013 as first published, but the 7.8% shown could reflect later revisions. The December 2012 figure was 7.8%, and the January 2013 release was 7.9%.

The 12-month change in unemployment of -0.7 fits too. January 2012 was 8.3% as published (8.5% originally), and 7.8 against 8.5 gives -0.7. I settle on January 2013.
